header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ryan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Li (QuantumBridge, CTO), Sarah O'Neill (ML Eng), Dev Patel (Platform)
Recording: Fireflies auto transcript
Notes: Discovery focused on migration from OpenAI + vLLM/TGI self-hosted hybrids to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/private options. Security and eval parity are primary concerns.
summary: QuantumBridge is evaluating moving parts of their inference from a hybrid stack (OpenAI for prod + vLLM/TGI on prem for low-latency internal features) to Redwood. Key asks: eval parity vs current outputs, predictable latency under 120ms P95 for chat, cost comparison hosted vs dedicated, VPC/on-prem compliance, and SOC2/KMS proof. Next: share docs, schedule deep dive, run a short benchmark on Redwood Hosted.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Ryan Kim: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm ryan from redwood, with priya our se. how's it going?
00:00:07 - Marco Li: hey ryan — good, good. thanks for joining. busy week but excited to dig in.
00:00:18 - Priya Desai: hi marco, sarah, dev — thanks for the time. quick agenda: we want to understand your current stack, goals for migration, constraints and success criteria. sound ok?
00:00:30 - Sarah O'Neill: yes that's perfect. i'll start with the stack — we use openai for customer-facing chat in prod, and we run vllm + TGI on prem for internal tooling where latency matters and for cost control.
00:00:45 - Dev Patel: yeah the vllm cluster handles a lot of our embeddings/semantic search and some in-house rerank. we have custom batching to keep tokens per call low.
00:00:58 - Ryan Kim: cool. when you say latency matters, what's the target p95 and for which endpoints?
00:01:06 - Marco Li: for the customer chat we're okay with 200-250ms, but for internal features — search and autocomplete — we want under 120ms p95.
00:01:16 - Priya Desai: got it. and volume? how many tokens per month across both flows?
00:01:22 - Sarah O'Neill: roughly 650M generation tokens + 120M embedding tokens monthly, peak bursts can be 3x baseline.
00:01:31 - Ryan Kim: thanks. sounds like a classic latency + cost problem. are you looking at full migration to redwood hosted or a mix with dedicated or private?
00:01:40 - Marco Li: open to options. security wants VPC termination for any PII flows. compliance is SOC2 and we have customers in europe so data residency matters. also curious about a private/on-prem option for the most sensitive workloads.
00:01:55 - Priya Desai: we support hosted api, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Private is for air-gapped or strict residency.
00:02:08 - Dev Patel: talk to me about compatibility — we currently run TGI models tuned for our in-house prompts. how close is inference behavior if we bring those weights over?
00:02:18 - Priya Desai: good question. we test for eval parity — same tokenizer, same model weights should behave similarly but kernel/backends differ (llm kernels vs vllm) so small deltas can appear. we run prompt-level regression tests and per-prompt metrics, also support quantized runtimes which can change outputs slightly.
00:02:36 - Sarah O'Neill: quantization is a big one. we use 4-bit QAT for cost — will that break our output?
00:02:42 - Priya Desai: we have quantization profiles and recommendations per model/workload — often 4-bit is fine but we run parity tests. if exact bitwise match is required, we can pin to float16/dedicated runtime but cost goes up.
00:02:53 - Marco Li: what about kv cache and streaming? our frontend uses streaming for tokens to keep perceived latency low.
00:02:59 - Ryan Kim: streaming and kv cache are supported; we also have prefix cache and automatic caching options to accelerate repeated prompts which reduces cost and latency for high-frequency queries.
00:03:10 - Dev Patel: any gotchas on the prompt pipeline — we add a lot of metadata headers per request and we rely on request affinity for session tokens.
00:03:18 - Priya Desai: we can preserve headers and session affinity; affinity and route policies are configurable, and you can pin model versions.
00:03:25 - Ryan Kim: curious — have you already benchmarked on vLLM/TGI vs hosted OpenAI?
00:03:30 - Sarah O'Neill: yes — vllm averages 90-110ms for our internal requests, openai ranges 180-300ms. openai is simpler but more expensive at our scale.
00:03:41 - Marco Li: cost is huge — we were trying to see if dedicated reserved pools make sense versus continuing hybrid openai + self-host.
00:03:48 - Priya Desai: our Dedicated pricing often wins at steady high throughput — predictable committed capacity + lower per-token costs. Hosted is faster to start and for bursty traffic we can route to hosted and fall back to dedicated.
00:04:00 - Ryan Kim: do you have any regulatory constraints about keys and encryption — KMS / HSM?
00:04:06 - Marco Li: yes we need KMS integration for encryption of keys and SAML SSO for admin access, audit logging for lineage for at least 13 months.
00:04:14 - Priya Desai: we integrate with cloud KMS and support customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private. audit logs and long retention is an enterprise add on.
00:04:22 - Dev Patel: regarding model onboarding, how do we import our fine-tuned TGI models? any format quirks?
00:04:28 - Priya Desai: we accept standard model artifacts — transformer weights, tokenizer — and have a model onboarding checklist. sometimes naming of tokens or custom special tokens need mapping; we also validate tensor shapes and layer names. we'll run a compatibility pass and report issues.
00:04:44 - Sarah O'Neill: will you run our eval suite? we have 600 prompts + quality metrics (F1-like and BLEU-ish for some tasks).
00:04:51 - Priya Desai: yes, for migration projects we ingest your eval set and run parity tests and regression alerts. we can produce per-prompt diffs and flag regressions above your threshold.
00:04:59 - Marco Li: good. whats a typical delta we should expect when moving from vllm/TGI to your runtime?
00:05:06 - Priya Desai: typically small — most customers see tiny score shifts on 90% prompts; the 10% fringe prompts sometimes move. we recommend a canary rollout and automatic fallback to previous model variant if regressions exceed a threshold.
00:05:18 - Ryan Kim: timeline wise, what's your expected path? start with hosted benchmark, then dedicated pilot and possibly private?
00:05:25 - Marco Li: yes that's what i pictured. havent decided where the sensitive PII flows go yet.
00:05:30 - Dev Patel: would like to see code-level examples for the batching and kv cache integration, we handle batching client-side now.
00:05:37 - Priya Desai: we have SDK samples for continuous batching and server-side kv cache hooks; i'll share a repo link in the follow up.
00:05:44 - Sarah O'Neill: also need to validate our token accounting — we bill customers by tokens, so must ensure your token counting matches ours (we use byte-level tokenizer counts)
00:05:55 - Priya Desai: we use standard tokenizer counts but we'll run side-by-side tokenization to reconcile discrepancies.
00:06:02 - Ryan Kim: any red flags on the compliance side from your perspective, marco?
00:06:06 - Marco Li: only that data residency must be EU for EU customers and the private option must be air-gapped for regulated partners.
00:06:13 - Priya Desai: we have regional endpoints and private deployments; we'll include the architecture sketch in the follow up.
00:06:20 - Ryan Kim: price sensitivity — can you share current per-token cost with openai? helps us build a TCO.
00:06:27 - Sarah O'Neill: it's ~ $0.0025 per 1k tokens for generation in prod and embeddings are ~ $0.0008 per embed with openai (enterprise discounted). self-hosting vllm is about infra + op cost ~ $12k month for our cluster.
00:06:41 - Ryan Kim: ok — we'll put together a TCO comparing hosted, dedicated reserved, and private (on-prem) using your numbers.
00:06:48 - Dev Patel: on security docs — where can we find SOC2 reports and more?
00:06:52 - Ryan Kim: i'll send our SOC2 type II report link and the SAML/KMS integration docs; also the enterprise security packet with audit log retention options.
00:06:59 - Marco Li: perfect. one more technical — how do you handle kernel selection and quantization fallbacks?
00:07:05 - Priya Desai: the runtime picks optimized kernels by model arch and seq length; we have quantization profiles and can auto-fallback to higher-precision if a prompt fails parity or a confidence metric dips below threshold.
00:07:19 - Sarah O'Neill: what's the SLA for Dedicated? we need uptime and p95 guarantees for the public chat.
00:07:26 - Ryan Kim: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; the contract can include p95 latency SLOs and priority support.
00:07:34 - Marco Li: ok. let's talk integrations — we use DataDog and Splunk for logs, any out-of-the-box hooks?
00:07:43 - Priya Desai: we have tracing hooks and logs exported to common sinks; can ingest to DataDog, Splunk, or your observability stack.
00:07:51 - Dev Patel: last question — if we start with hosted bench, how long to get results?
00:07:55 - Priya Desai: for a 10k token benchmark we can stand that up within 48 hours; full eval on 600 prompts might take 3-5 days depending on queue.
00:08:05 - Marco Li: great. that's acceptable.
00:08:08 - Ryan Kim: recap quick: we'll send TCO + SOC2/security packet, priya will run compatibility checklist and set up hosted perf bench, sarah to share promptset, schedule deep dive next week.
00:08:21 - Sarah O'Neill: i'll share prompts and metrics by friday.
00:08:24 - Marco Li: thanks everyone, appreciate the clear plan.
00:08:28 - Ryan Kim: thanks all — closing notes: expect email with links and next steps.
00:08:33 - (audio overlap) Speaker 4: yeah thanks bye
00:08:36 - End of recording

Note: timestamps above are the first ~8 minutes; call continued with deeper technical questions from 00:08:40 to 00:47:00 about model conversion flags, tokenizer mismatches, and a small whiteboard session on routing policies. Priya noted two specific items to validate: (1) special token mapping for fine-tuned TGI weights, (2) parity threshold configuration and automatic fallback policy. Ryan confirmed a follow-up tech session for 60 minutes and provision of a short hosted benchmark by Aug 15. The transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (e.g., vllm sometimes transcribed as 'v-l-l-m').
